factors.title: Low Volatility in High VIX Regimes
factors.hypothesis: The low-volatility anomaly suggests that stocks with lower idiosyncratic risk tend to outperform. This effect is often more pronounced during periods of market stress or uncertainty, as indicated by a high VIX. In such environments, investors may flock to perceived safe-haven assets, driving up their prices. Therefore, stocks with relatively low volatility during periods of elevated market-wide fear should generate higher returns.
